subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Environmental Nudges
description: A fast breakdown of Environmental Nudges for builders.

hook.text: Double-sided printing set as default at a university saved 4.6 million sheets in one semester. One setting change.

buildup.text: Environmental nudges reduce waste, energy, and emissions by redesigning the default behavior, not by preaching.

discovery.text: Footprints on the ground leading to trash cans reduce litter by 46%. Make the right behavior the path of least.

twist.text: Carbon labels on food affect behavior only when they're simple: red/yellow/green, not grams. Complexity kills the nudge.

climax.text: Environmental nudges succeed because they ask nothing of people. The environment changes.

punchline.text: Save the planet by changing the defaults.

quiz.question: Why did default double-sided printing save so much paper?
options: People were forced to print less
Most people never changed the default setting

details.summary: Environmental nudges modify the physical environment to steer behavior without any verbal messaging. Making stairs more attractive than elevators, placing healthy food at eye level, and using smaller plates all nudge behavior through environmental design rather than persuasion.
details.whyItMatters: Environmental nudges are powerful because they operate below conscious awareness and require no literacy, comprehension, or motivation from the person being nudged.
takeaways: Physical environment modifications can change behavior without conscious awareness
Environmental nudges work continuously and require no motivation from the target
Proximity, visibility, and ease of access are the three main levers

faq.question: What are effective examples of environmental nudges?
faq.answer: Placing fruit at eye level and candy below the counter in cafeterias. Painting attractive stairwell art to encourage stair use. Reducing plate size to lower portion sizes. Placing recycling bins closer than trash cans. Each changes default behavior through physical arrangement.

faq.question: Why are environmental nudges more effective than informational campaigns?
faq.answer: Information campaigns require attention, comprehension, motivation, and sustained effort. Environmental nudges change the path of least resistance so that the desired behavior becomes the easiest option. They work even when people are distracted or unmotivated.
